panel.evidence: `update()` passes the raw request body straight through: `data: body` (api/v1/documents.controller.ts:77-80). The parameter is annotated with an inline TS type (`@Body() body: { title?: string }`), so the emitted `design:paramtypes` metadata is `Object` and the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:59-66, `whitelist`/`forbidNonWhitelisted`) skips validation entirely — those options only strip properties when the metatype is a decorated DTO class. Prisma accepts any valid `DocumentUpdateInput` at runtime, so an authenticated caller scoped to workspace A can PATCH one of its own documents with e.g. `{"workspace":{"connect":{"id":"<victim-workspace-id>"}}}` (moving attacker-controlled content into a workspace they are not a member of — WorkspaceScopeGuard only checks the route param, not the body), or `{"author":{"connect":{"id":1}}}` to forge authorship, or overwrite `id`/`fileId`. The sibling legacy route (document/document.controller.ts:183-196) does the safe thing and copies allowlisted fields; this one does not. The diff modifies `DocumentService.updateDocument` (document.service.ts:99-101) without narrowing this sink.
